o.text: From Proto-Turkic *köri-, *köŕ- (“to see, look”). Azerbaijani göz (“eye”) is equally derived from the Proto-Turkic root *kör- (“to see, look”) according to the regular sound change of /ŕ/ to /z/ in Common Turkic, whereas this shift did not occur in Azerbaijani görmək and its cognate verbs in other Turkic languages, such as Old Turkic 𐰚𐰇𐰼 (kör-, “to see”), Turkish görmek (“to see”), Kazakh көру (körüw, “to see”), Uzbek koʻrmoq (“to see”), etc. The Proto-Turkic verb is derived from the Proto-Turkic word *kȫŕ “eye”.
From Proto-Common Turkic *kač- (“to run away, flee”). Cognate with Turkish kaçmak etc.
Calque of Russian призывни́к (prizyvník). By surface analysis, çağırış + -çı.

Etymology tree

Arabic نَهْر (nahr)bor.?
Proto-Semitic *nahar-
Aramaic נהראbor.?

Borrowed from Persian نهره (nahra), presumably from Arabic نَهْر (nahr, “river”) or either. Doublet of nəhr (now outdated) and Nehrəm.
